name: Avanti Feeds Ltd
tagline: Quality shrimp-feed leader whose biggest recent catalyst -- a US tariff cut on Indian shrimp -- has already played out in the stock, which broke its all-time high and roughly doubled
business_overview: Avanti Feeds is India's leading shrimp feed manufacturer, also processing and exporting shrimp, with a joint venture into pet food (with Thailand's Bluefalo) as a diversification move.
fundamentals_narrative: ROCE (24.4%) and ROE (18.3%) are genuinely strong and the balance sheet is clean, but revenue growth (8.15% CAGR) is modest -- this is a high-quality, mature compounder rather than a fast-growing small-cap. At an already-Rs 11,547 Cr market cap, the size itself is a headwind to a 10x-in-2-3-years framing.
technical_read: Not independently pulled -- the forum thread itself documents the stock breaking its all-time high and nearly doubling in a two-week window around Feb 2026.
sentiment_summary: Read the 50 most recent posts (#2487-2538, spanning Jan 2025 to Jun 2026) of a very large, long-running thread (2,538 posts total). Multiple trusted users (Rahul_Behera, VALUE2017, UrsRafeek, all elevated-tier) actively tracked policy and input-cost news through the period.
community_signal: The dominant catalyst in the recent thread: in February 2026, the US cut import duties on Indian shrimp from ~50% to ~18%, which Rahul_Behera (trusted) flagged as handing back ~32% of value to the supply chain -- the stock broke its all-time high and nearly doubled within two weeks. thakurvi (non-trusted but active, high-love) had booked profit at Rs 938 back in March 2025 after a prior 398-to-938 run, showing this is a stock with a history of sharp moves followed by profit-taking. UrsRafeek (trusted) more recently (May 2026) flagged a 20% domestic feed-price hike as a separate, unrelated cost dynamic worth watching.
bse_notes: Not checked this pass -- no red-flag corporate actions surfaced.
bull_case: Genuinely strong ROCE (24.4%) and ROE (18.3%) with a clean, low-debt balance sheet
Real, structural tailwind from the Feb 2026 US tariff cut on Indian shrimp exports, which materially improves industry economics
Category leadership and a new pet-food JV as a diversification option
bear_case: The single biggest identified catalyst (the tariff cut) has already been priced in -- the stock broke its ATH and nearly doubled on the news months before this pass
Revenue growth (8.15% CAGR) is modest for a company already at Rs 11,547 Cr market cap -- a 10x from here would require an unusually large re-rating on top of an already-large base
A recent domestic feed-price hike (flagged May 2026) is a fresh cost headwind not yet reflected in the fundamentals data pulled this pass
verdict_headline: A genuinely high-quality shrimp-feed leader, but the market cap and the fact that its main catalyst already fired make this a poor fit for a 10x-in-2-3-years thesis from here
verdict_reasoning: ROCE/ROE and balance-sheet quality are excellent and the US tariff-cut catalyst was real, not speculative -- this is a genuinely good business

But that catalyst has already driven the stock to an all-time high and roughly doubled it, and the company's underlying growth rate (8% CAGR) is too slow to support another multibagger move from an already-Rs 11,500 Cr base without a fresh, undiscovered catalyst
Conviction is set to Medium reflecting real business quality, with thesis_fit as neither given size and the already-realized catalyst

four_box.note: US tariff cut on Indian shrimp exports (Feb-2026) is a genuine structural tailwind for the industry; modest 8.15% revenue CAGR at an already-Rs11,547cr base — tam no; category leadership + new pet-food JV is a modest diversification edge — weak; the tariff-cut catalyst already drove the stock to an ATH (nearly doubled) before this pass — valuation no.
